AfterRoomEntered.maps_to: no counterpart (the sim's Relic.after_room_entered is not implemented by this port)
AfterRoomEntered.rationale: Pantograph.cs:16-25's entire body is a status assignment: it looks one step ahead on the map (`Map.BossMapPoint.parents.Contains(CurrentMapPoint)`) and lights the relic up when the next room could be the boss. Presentation only -- the heal itself is decided independently at BeforeCombatStart by reading the CURRENT room's type, so no state crosses between the two hooks. The port's docstring says as much and is correct. RelicModel.Flash(), base.Status = RelicStatus.* and InvokeDisplayAmountChanged() are presentation only (the relic card's glow, its greyed/active state and its counter in the relic bar); the sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim -- the same verdict audit/records/relic/unsettling_lamp.json N5 and audit/records/relic/belt_buckle.json N1 give RelicStatus writes (binding rule 3).

BeforeCombatStart.maps_to: on_combat_start (pantograph.py:21-26), dispatched by CombatState at combat setup
BeforeCombatStart.rationale: Pantograph.cs:27-34: `!base.Owner.Creature.IsDead && base.Owner.RunState.CurrentRoom.RoomType == RoomType.Boss` then `CreatureCmd.Heal(base.Owner.Creature, base.DynamicVars.Heal.BaseValue)`. CanonicalVars is `new HealVar(25m)` (line 14) with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so HEAL = 25 (pantograph.py:19) is the pinned non-ascension value. The sim reads `self.combat.room_type` instead of RunState.CurrentRoom.RoomType, which the driver sets from the room being entered (see N1). The IsDead guard is structurally satisfied -- the player cannot enter a combat dead, and CreatureCmd.heal bails on a dead target anyway (cmds.py:532-560, re-verified 2026-08-04 after line drift). Slot: BeforeCombatStart maps to on_combat_start, which `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order` prints BEFORE the turn-1 block clear, i.e. before anything can read the healed HP.

guards.what: N1: the room-type gate. `RunState.CurrentRoom.RoomType == RoomType.Boss` (Pantograph.cs:29) vs `self.combat.room_type != RoomType.BOSS` (pantograph.py:23) -- does the sim's driver actually populate room_type?
guards.rationale: EXECUTED rather than assumed, because binding rule 5 forbids resting a faithful verdict on an unverified premise and a relic gated on an unset field would be silently inert. `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py pantograph-boss` shows both drivers passing it -- driver.py:507 and conformance/runner.py:236 are each `run.create_combat(encounter, room_type=room_type)` -- and then drives the relic through all four values: room_type None / MONSTER / ELITE leave a 40-HP player at 40, and BOSS takes them to 65 (40 + 25, capped by an 80 max). CombatState stores the value at combat.py:166 (constructor default at :135) with a docstring naming room-gated relics as its consumers. NOTE per binding rule 7: the rationale leans on sts2_rl/driver.py, sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py and sts2_rl/combat.py, none of which this record hashes. (2026-08-04: all three files had drifted; re-ran the cited probe, output unchanged.)

guards.what: N2: the heal is capped at max HP on both sides
guards.rationale: CreatureCmd.Heal clamps to MaxHp, and the sim's CreatureCmd.heal (cmds.py:532-560) does the same and returns the HP actually restored. So a near-full-HP player gains less than 25 identically on both sides. Checked because a relic that healed past the cap would be observable on the very first boss.
